evidence_items.summary: Choosing a network architecture for zero-knowledge (ZK) proofs of inference needs a circuit-cost estimate that can be checked against the prover, yet NAS work on ZK has relied on untested cost proxies. We study ezkl, a Halo2-based prover, on CIFAR-10 MLPs, CNNs and ResNet-style networks. (1) Cost model. A parametric model of assigned cells, with coefficients fitted on 180 trained, calibrated networks and evaluated on 54 held-out ones, matches ezkl-calibrated logrows exactly for 39 and within one for 51 (Spearman 0.84; cross-validated over all 234 networks: 70% exact, 95% within one). The mismatches have a mechanism: on 72 dumped ezkl settings, logrows is exactly the maximum of four resource requirements (rows, constants, lookup table, range-check table; 72 of 72 sampled networks at logrows 19–23), of which cell count is one. (2) A negative result. Width-matched, ReLU and x² networks have the same calibrated logrows (all 5 skeletons; 45 of 50 matched pairs in the sweep), contradicting the assumption that polynomial activations are cheaper to prove in ezkl; unnormalized x³ + x networks calibrate to a circuit up to 16× larger at equal cell count because their range-check table spans 2²² + 1 values. (3) Benchmark. We release zkml-bench, 474 networks with two training seeds and proxy scores. NEAR predicts accuracy only for ReLU networks (ρ = +0.70) and is indistinguishable from zero on all three polynomial families; a Zen-style score (our variant, not the published Zen-Score protocol) is anti-correlated on polynomial networks; a sign-pattern NASWOT variant is negatively correlated on polynomial networks; ZiCo’s apparent success on x³ + x disappears once failed training runs are removed. Between 39% and 60% of polynomial networks fail to train. (4) Search.
evidence_items.title: ZK-Circuit-Aware NAS: A Cost Model, Benchmark, and Proxy Study for Provable Inference

evidence_items.summary: Background/Objectives: This study internally evaluated deep learning models for classifying mandibular condylar position on sagittal cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) images using a predefined joint-space-based reference standard. Methods: In this single-center retrospective study, 1040 temporomandibular joint images from 560 patients were categorized as anterior, centric, or posterior using Pullinger and Hollender’s method. Patients were allocated to training, validation, and test sets in an 80:10:10 ratio (448, 56, and 56 patients, respectively), yielding 823, 107, and 110 joint images. Three object-detection models (YOLOv8x, YOLOv8n, and RF-DETR Nano) were evaluated on the same test set for condylar region localization and position classification. Performance was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and mean average precision (mAP). Results: YOLOv8x correctly classified 97 of 110 test images, achieving an accuracy of 0.88 (patient-cluster bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.81–0.95) and an mAP@0.5 of 0.89. YOLOv8n and RF-DETR Nano correctly classified 84 and 82 images, with accuracies of 0.76 and 0.75 and mAP@0.5 values of 0.80 and 0.81, respectively. The mAP@0.5:0.95 values for YOLOv8n and RF-DETR Nano were 0.60 and 0.59, respectively. YOLOv8x’s mAP@0.5:0.95 was 0.66. For YOLOv8x, recall/F1-score were highest for anterior class (0.94/0.91) and lowest for centric class (0.79/0.83), with precision ranging from 0.88 to 0.89 across classes. Intra- and inter-observer classification agreement in 156 joints was κ = 0.90 and 0.97, respectively. Conclusions: The YOLOv8x-based model achieved the highest overall accuracy among the three models in this comparison, indicating that it can classify mandibular condylar position on sagittal CBCT images according to predefined categories.
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence–Based Classification of Mandibular Condylar Position Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Single-Center Internal Evaluation

evidence_items.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) now generate patches, call tools, retrieve context, and iterate on test feedback, yet published gains are usually reported as counts of patches that pass a test suite on public benchmarks. This review asks whether retrieval-augmented and agentic designs yield more independently correct repairs at comparable cost. Journal articles issued from 2022 to 2026 were retrieved from the OpenAIRE Graph and Crossref with the full Boolean string, supplemented by title screening where abstracts were unavailable. A three-layer design combined a bibliometric map of 151 articles, an abstract-level evidence map and technical appraisal of 67 core empirical studies (11 in full text), and a structured synthesis of matched within-study contrasts. Output grew from 19 articles in 2024 to 83 in 2026, concentrated in five software engineering venues. Coupling analysis separated learning-based repair, agentic repository-level repair, and patch-validity research, with weak modularity indicating a shared intellectual base dominated by Defects4J. Agents, retrieval, and repository-level tasks rose sharply between 2024-2025 and 2026, whereas attention to contamination and patch correctness stayed flat. Only 11% of core abstracts mentioned the plausible versus correct distinction and 11% addressed contamination. Seven studies yielded ten matched contrasts; the nine with magnitudes showed relative gains of 6% to 56%, but none reported paired discordant outcomes or variances, so no pooled estimate was defensible. Memorization and production evidence indicate that benchmark gains overstate deployable correctness. The review proposes a minimum reporting set built on paired per-bug outcomes, budget parity, independent oracles, and contamination audits.
evidence_items.title: A bibliometric review, systematic evidence synthesis, and structured quantitative synthesis of retrieval-augmented and agentic large language models for software repair

evidence_items.summary: An agent that stores facts over time eventually stores several versions of the same fact. Asked a value-agnostic question - "which team does X play for now?" - a similarity retriever cannot prefer the current version, because every version matches the entity the query names. StaleBench isolates this stale-retrieval failure on 892 real updating facts, with currency labels from the source (Wikidata validity years via TempLAMA), never from a retrieval score. Our central result is that retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards: a retention policy and its retain-everything control return the identical statement at rank 1 for every test query, yet differ by 29.5 and 65.6 points in reader accuracy on two readers when no date is shown. Contamination@5, the metric we add, ranks them correctly where current@1 and current@5 do not. Withdrawing the lexical anchor that statements carry costs deployed keying mechanisms tens of points of freshness; entity resolution on both the write path and the query recovers most of the loss. Three deployed systems (Mem0, Graphiti, LangMem) and a reimplemented ERASE each handle supersession differently, and no single scoring convention describes all four. We release the data, a frozen evaluator, and reference baselines.
evidence_items.title: StaleBench: Isolating Stale Retrieval in Agent Memory, and Pricing the Fix

evidence_items.summary: Background: However, naturally occurring iron enrichment in groundwater poses significant challenges to water quality and public health. Objective: This study assessed the concentration levels of iron in selected borehole water sources within Ikot Abasi Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria, examined compliance with World Health Organization (WHO) drinking-water standards, evaluated the spatial distribution of iron contamination, and investigated the potential public health implications associated with long-term consumption of iron-contaminated water. Methods: A cross-sectional environmental assessment was adopted involving field sampling, laboratory analysis, Geographic Information System (GIS)-based spatial mapping, and household surveys. Forty-five borehole water samples were collected from fifteen communities and analyzed for iron concentration using Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometry (AAS). All sampled communities exceeded the WHO recommended limit of 0.30 mg/L for drinking water. Survey findings showed that residents commonly experienced water discoloration, metallic taste, staining of household items, pipe blockage, and increased reliance on alternative water sources. Results: The results revealed that iron concentrations ranged from 0.43 mg/L to 2.31 mg/L, with an overall mean concentration of 1.11 mg/L. Spatial analysis identified major contamination hotspots in Okoroete, Utaewa, Edemaya, Essene, and Akata communities, indicating significant geographical variation in iron occurrence. Conclusion: Groundwater derived from boreholes constitutes the principal source of domestic water supply for many households in the Niger Delta region of Nigeria.
evidence_items.title: Elevated Iron Levels in Borehole Water within abandoned Nigeria Aluminium Company (ALSCON) and Associated Public Health Implications: A Case Study of Ikot Abasi Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State, Nigeria

evidence_items.summary: This cross-sectional survey examined associations between four school counselling strategies and student-reported parent–teen relationships in public secondary schools in Asaba, Delta State, Nigeria. The sampling frame comprised 9,128 senior secondary students in nine schools. Of 383 questionnaires administered, 338 were usable (88.25%). Students rated individual counselling, group counselling, communication skills training, family-oriented guidance and parent–teen relationships on a five-point scale. Frequencies, means, standard deviations, Pearson correlations and multiple regression were reported. Communication skills training received the highest mean rating (4.09) and had the largest positive bivariate correlation with parent–teen relationships (r = .673). Individual counselling, group counselling and communication skills training had positive coefficients in the supplied regression table, while the family-oriented guidance coefficient had p = .128. The supplied correlation and regression summaries require reconciliation against the original output before the adjusted associations can be interpreted conclusively. The descriptive findings identify communication skills training as a priority for further evaluation in school counselling programmes.
evidence_items.title: COUNSELLING STRATEGIES AND PARENT–TEEN RELATIONSHIPS IN PUBLIC SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN ASABA, DELTA STATE

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI) are increasingly recognised as important considerations in research policy and practice, with implications for achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This viewpoint examines EDI through two interconnected dimensions: equitable participation and opportunities within research systems, and the integration of EDI into the conduct of research. The first concerns how institutional practices, employment conditions, funding arrangements, and research assessment influence access to research careers, professional progression, and recognition. The second concerns how research priorities, methodologies, partnerships, and dissemination practices affect whose perspectives are represented, whose contributions are valued, and who benefits from research. While governments, research funders, and research performing organisations have introduced policies and initiatives to advance EDI, their effectiveness depends on implementation, coordination, and evaluation. Drawing on existing frameworks such as the Athena Swan Charter, the Agreement on Reforming Research Assessment, and UNESCO’s Recommendation on Open Science, the viewpoint argues that progress requires coordinated system leadership extending beyond individual institutional commitments. It proposes that funders and research performing organisations jointly review how funding conditions, employment arrangements, and assessment criteria affect equitable opportunities, and agree on a proportionate set of shared outcome indicators. The SDGs provide a basis for aligning these responsibilities with wider objectives concerning reduced inequalities, accountable institutions, and inclusive knowledge production.
evidence_items.title: Equality, Diversity and Inclusion in SDG-Aligned Research Systems: The Case for Coordinated System Leadership

evidence_items.summary: This research poster examines inaccuracies and potential biases in automated transcription and de-identification of primary care encounters through Project HEAL (Healthcare Encounter Annotation and Labelling) at the University of Washington. The study explores the types of errors these systems produce and their potential clinical and ethical implications. AI-generated transcripts, produced using Microsoft transcription software and processed through Microsoft Presidio for de-identification, were compared with human-reviewed and corrected transcripts. The research team qualitatively identified recurring errors and collectively developed categories describing transcription inaccuracies, censorship of medically relevant language, and failures in identifying or removing sensitive information. Identified error categories include speech-to-text misinterpretations, profanity filtering of clinical terms, transcription errors that trigger incorrect de-identification, incorrect entity classification, under-redaction, and inconsistent de-identification. Examples illustrate challenges involving African American Language, brand names, and sexual health terminology. These errors can alter clinically meaningful information, introduce bias, and compromise privacy. The poster highlights the importance of meaningful human review and healthcare-specific evaluation of transcription and de-identification pipelines. Findings identify areas for improvement in the accuracy, fairness, and reliability of AI-supported clinical documentatio
evidence_items.title: Inaccuracies and Biases of AI Scribes in Healthcare

evidence_items.summary: AetherHuman is a candidate eleventh functional dimension of the Aether family. v1.0.0 is an architectural investigation of the human participation gap between governance authority (AetherGovern), identity (AetherIdentity), and runtime monitoring (AetherRuntime). Links: - Paper (v1.0.0): https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24278322 - Figshare preprint: https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.35038726 - GitHub: https://github.com/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - GitLab: https://gitlab.com/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - Codeberg: https://codeberg.org/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - Bitbucket: https://bitbucket.org/gitdeeper15/aetherhuman - Website: https://aetherhuman.netlify.app What v1.0.0 contains: - 5 functions under investigation (Fn1–Fn5): Human Principal Representation, Authority Relation, Intervention Semantics, Accountability Chain, Human-Agent Boundary. - 4 failure conditions (H-F1–H-F4): Non-redundancy, Distinction from Govern + Identity + Runtime, Decentralizability, Observable benefit. - 2 propositions (P1–P2): Determinism of human intervention semantics, Irreducible human authority anchor. - Architectural hypothesis, responsibility boundaries, falsification plan, independence decision, internal review, and investigation report. - 9 figures (Fig1–Fig9). - No implementation, no tests, no experiments. What v1.0.0 does not claim: - AetherHuman is not confirmed. - H-F1–H-F4 are not all "not falsified". - P1–P2 are not proven. - The architecture is not production-ready. - The gap is not genuine. No implementation has been evaluated. H-F1, H-F2, H-F3 are not falsified by argument; H-F2 is most fragile; H-F4 remains untested. P1–P2 remain proof sketches, not machine-checked. evidence_items.summary: The goal of this deliverable is to provide an overview of the current implementation of the Synthetic Populations Generator (SPG), a service developed in the framework of the FOSSR project for the extraction of synthetic populations. These are a class of algorithms for the extraction of statistical properties of a population from aggregated or separated data. This is a critical challenge when micro-level data is not available due to privacy concerns or information being scattered over different datasets. Identify such micro-level information can benefit quantitative and simulation methods for the study of population dynamics such as agent-based modelling. The goal of SPG is to support researchers and policymakers with a friendly service to extract micro-level information from aggregated data. To this aim, the algorithm implements a general product rule of joint probabilities from marginal data identified from the input data and adjusting for joint counts provided by the user. The output of the service is a table containing the number of individuals for each intersection profile, iterative also by space units. Furthermore, users can download a script for agent-based modelling ready to be initialized with the same table extracted for the creation of the synthetic population. Aligning with the Open Science framework, the service is delivered through three channels. Open code developed in Python is accessible through a GitHub repository, a local demo is available, and the service also runs through a web-app in the Virtual Research Environment (VRE) developed by FOSSR-Lab. The three modalities align with the Open Science perspective of the FOSSR project and are envisaged to facilitate future integrations of the service in the FOSSR cloud in the future.

evidence_items.summary: Code and data for a maximum-likelihood spectral analysis of the two gamma-ray glow cores (glow A and glow B) measured on 2023-07-29 by the University of Bergen BGO detector (UIB-BGO) on board NASA's ER-2 aircraft during the ALOFT campaign. For each glow core, the analysis compares the measured counts with Geant4 photon-transport templates folded through the detector response. It uses a Poisson signal-plus-background likelihood, profiles the signal amplitude and a bounded background factor, and evaluates every supported cell of the source geometry grid (source altitude, horizontal offset from the aircraft nadir, glow radius). Compatible geometry sets are calibrated with Poisson mock spectra (10,000 per cell) instead of asymptotic thresholds. The record contains: - the analysis code (Python: NumPy, SciPy, Numba), its configuration, tests and a pinned environment file; - the photon-transport templates for source altitudes of 12 to 16 km, on a grid of offsets and glow radii from 0 to 8 km in 0.5 km steps; - the UIB-BGO response-matrix database and BGO energy calibration (identical to the Bayesian MCMC Glow Spectral Analysis https://zenodo.org/records/23695652); - normal-event spectra of the two glow cores and of a 711 s quiet background of the same flight, in 63 measured energy bins from 300 keV to 40 MeV, with the background selection record; - the results: full likelihood grids, calibrated p-values, compatible sets, validation (coverage, exact-search and background-sensitivity checks) and the paired figure. Raw photon-by-photon detector data and navigation files are not included. The README documents how to rerun the fits, the figure, the validation and the tests. Claude AI was used to assist in writing the documentation and the beautifying the plots and figures.
evidence_items.title: Maximum Likelihood spectral analysis of airborne gamma-ray glow observations, with the UIB-BGO response matrix and the ER-2 GDML mass model

evidence_items.summary: Raw audit data, tables and reproduction scripts for a controlled protocol audit of adaptive-weight (online) forecast-combination evaluation. The standard overlapping-sliding-window protocol (stride = 1) inflates reported gains; decoupled experiments attribute the decay primarily to controller feedback delay (82-109% of the joint effect) rather than evaluation-denominator double counting. Dose response: monotone decay, zero crossing at stride 4-64, half-life 4-8 windows; at the honest wall-clock endpoint gains are -0.1% to -5.7% in the seven audited cells, with 6/7 95% CI upper bounds at or below 0 (the seventh interval is -0.257, +0.08, point estimate still negative); the only positive non-overlapping endpoint found is one cell of a GPN-augmented pool (+0.77%). Bit-for-bit fidelity checks (14/14) against canonical internal tables. Sentinel controls reported for every cell: oracle upper bound (never exceeded), non-overlapping re-evaluation, cold-start bias. Framework priority (evaluation-sampling vs feedback-timing separation, feedback-lag dose-response curve, sentinel trio) is established by this deposit date; the forecasting engine and its theory belong to a sister manuscript under review and are cited, not claimed, here. 本记录为自适应权重(在线)预测组合常用评测协议(重叠滑窗,stride=1)的审计证据包。解耦实验表明:标准协议下的控制器增益随反馈/评测步长增大而单调衰减,在 stride 4-64 间归零反号(半衰期 4-8 窗);归因上衰减主要由控制器反馈滞后驱动(解释联合衰减的 82-109%),而非评点分母重复计数(仅抽分母时增益变化在 ±3.5 个百分点内)。保真校验 14/14 逐位复现同族工作定案表。本记录仅确立上述归因框架的时间戳优先权,引擎与理论归同作者另一在审稿件。
evidence_items.title: Audit data for evaluation-protocol dependence in adaptive-weight online forecast combination: window overlap, feedback delay, and gain attribution

evidence_items.summary: Esta presentación describe el desarrollo de un sistema de generación aumentada por recuperación (RAG) para consultar datos arqueológicos de IDEArq, la Infraestructura de Datos Espaciales de Investigación Arqueológica, alojada en la infraestructura de datos EXEA del CCHS-CSIC. El corpus incluye 525 artículos científicos (2000-2024) en cinco idiomas y una capa GeoJSON con 4.478 yacimientos con dataciones de radiocarbono. Se detalla la arquitectura del sistema (indexación en chunks, embeddings multilingües, recuperación vectorial, híbrida y multiquery, reranking y modelos de lenguaje de pequeño tamaño ejecutados en local) y su evaluación con la métrica MRR y el marco RAGAS. Los resultados muestran que la recuperación vectorial no basta para todas las consultas: los fragmentos de texto desplazan a los registros de yacimientos, y el modelo inventa o aproxima distancias y fechas. Como solución se propone una arquitectura con un router determinista y dos rutas: una documental, enriquecida con un grafo bibliográfico RDF/SPARQL, y una espacial, con filtros sobre el GeoJSON y cálculos geográficos auditables en Python. Esta última permite, por ejemplo, recuperar los 10 yacimientos esperados en un radio de 30 km de Jaén, frente a los 2 que devolvía la búsqueda solo con embeddings. Para mejorar la ruta espacial, actualmente se encuentra en desarrollo un agente que utiliza una interfaz de línea de comandos en Python, determinista y no basada en un LLM, que realiza los cálculos con las bibliotecas GeoPandas, Shapely y PyProj. El LLM del agente, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, se limita a elegir la operación, leer el resultado y redactar la respuesta, y el comando ejecutado se muestra para poder auditar el cálculo.
evidence_items.title: Descubriendo el pasado con inteligencia artificial: un sistema RAG para datos arqueológicos

evidence_items.summary: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. To address these challenges, we introduce LynnReal-Hand, a hand-controlled video world model that unifies precise interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation. We curate 100K interaction clips spanning diverse real and synthetic environments and develop hand-aware supervision to improve fine-grained hand motions and object interactions. Building on this foundation, we learn a causal flow map for few-step generation and introduce region-aware score distillation that combines complementary video and image priors to refine interaction dynamics and visual appearance. To further reduce inference latency, we propose Ultra-Fast-VAE, a compact video decoder that preserves high reconstruction fidelity with substantially lower computational cost. Extensive evaluations on HandBench demonstrate superior hand-following accuracy and visual quality compared with existing approaches. Our full-sequence model achieves an FVD of 181.67 and a MANO Dice score of 93.02, while the three-step causal model maintains a MANO Dice score of 92.49. For real-time interaction, 540p streaming on a single H200 reaches 18.03 FPS with 741ms latency and an optimized peak GPU memory footprint of only 34.89GB. We will release the datasets, model weights, and the full training and inference code to support research on hand-controlled video world models.
evidence_items.title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control

evidence_items.summary: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index, with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered. A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost. These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection. Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.
evidence_items.title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare

evidence_items.summary: Can a vision-language model look at a picture of a chain reaction and tell what will happen? Recent multimodal models describe scenes fluently and solve textbook physics problems, which suggests they should also predict how a scene of ramps, ledges, pendulums, seesaws and dominoes plays out once a ball is pushed. We tested this claim on 30 models from 10 families and reached a clear conclusion: unaided, no model predicts the outcome reliably. We built DominoBench, a benchmark of still images of 2D rigid-body scenes whose outcome a physics simulator computes. It holds 854 items in 427 minimal pairs, in which a change of one to three grid steps in one quantity decides whether one person survives, and every item comes with a four-rung hint ladder ending in the exact calculation that decides the outcome. Unaided, frontier models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI are right about the person whose fate flips in at most 72% of items and answer both twins of a pair correctly in at most 34%. Pointing at the deciding step helps little, and exact geometry given as text barely helps, yet once the deciding calculation and the quantities it needs, including speeds that a still image cannot show, are written out, the same models reach 82-92% on the deciding person, while small open-weight models stay near chance. Physical prediction from a still image therefore fails at the quantitative step: the strongest models use the deciding quantity when they are given it, but do not produce it on their own. For models that plan or act in the physical world, a fluent account of a scene is thus no evidence of a correct prediction: such models must find and compute the deciding quantity unprompted, and DominoBench tests whether they do.
evidence_items.title: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images

evidence_items.summary: As technological innovation accelerates, patent drafting remains time-consuming and highly dependent on professional expertise. This study proposes a patent text generation framework that identifies technological gaps from existing patent knowledge and generates patentable drafts. The framework establishes an ontology-based domain structure, applies a Technology–Function Matrix (TFM) to identify high-potential technology–function pairings, and uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to transform these pairings into invention concepts. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and prompt engineering are then integrated into a modular workflow for generating abstracts, titles, figure descriptions, claims, and IPC classifications. Sustainable energy storage is selected as the case domain due to its growing importance in net-zero transitions and renewable energy integration. The generated texts are evaluated using vector-based semantic similarity and Precision, Recall, and F1-score metrics. By integrating patent mining, text mining, and domain-specific technology–function analysis, the proposed framework supports transdisciplinary engineering practice and bridge engineering design, knowledge discovery, and sustainable innovation, demonstrating the practical applicability of data-driven artificial intelligence in patent text generation.
evidence_items.title: Using Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Model for Novel Patent Generation

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are rapidly entering translator education, yet it remains unclear whether they build students' own translation competence or merely improve the products students submit. We combined a validation study on public benchmark data with a 16-week quasi-experiment to test a scaffolded human--LLM pedagogy, the Draft--Diagnose--Revise--Reflect (D2R) cycle, for English--Chinese translation. In Study 1, a rubric-guided error-annotation prompt increased the agreement between LLM feedback and expert Multidimensional Quality Metrics judgements on 2,500 WMT segments for all four models tested; with this prompt GPT-4o reached a segment-level Kendall's $\tau$ of 0.30, on a par with the strongest neural metric, and the highest error-detection accuracy. In Study 2, 179 English majors received conventional instruction, unrestricted LLM access or the guardrailed D2R cycle. Unrestricted access maximised LLM-assisted performance but yielded no advantage in unassisted translation over conventional instruction at a delayed test 12 weeks after the course (Hedges' $g$ = $-$0.08) and produced the largest AI-dependency gap. Scaffolded use produced durable gains in unassisted translation ($g$ = 0.70), a 13\% reduction in error rate and higher metacognitive regulation. Process logs indicated that the benefit was transmitted mainly through lower verbatim adoption of LLM output. Pedagogical design, not LLM access per se, determines whether LLMs support or supplant translation learning.
evidence_items.title: Scaffolded large language model feedback builds durable translation competence whereas unrestricted use fosters dependency

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Clinical registries capture adverse events (AEs) in free-text fields that are rarely analyzed. We developed a reproducible large language model (LLM)-assisted workflow using 11,216 free-text entries from 18,069 patients in the German Stroke Registry; 9,146 informative entries were retained after filtering. Embedding-based clustering showed poor separation, whereas an LLM-guided taxonomy identified 89 leaf labels. On the model-assisted 1,000-entry development set used for model and prompt selection, GPT-5.4 reached F1 92.4% (95% confidence interval [CI] 91.4-93.4). On 300 held-out entries, weighted F1 against clinician consensus was 96.5% (94.6-98.1) for frozen GPT-5.4 labels and 90.5% (87.5-93.5) for locally run Qwen 3.5 27B. For AE concepts with a comparable structured field, free text documented 1,345 additional instances (+19.6% over 6,867 structured instances); it also documented 7,546 instances of AE concepts without a structured equivalent, most often pneumonia, urinary tract infection and delirium. Beyond baseline covariates and the structured AE count, integrated complication concepts increased the area under the curve for prediction of good functional outcome by 0.025 (95% CI 0.021-0.028) and for death by 0.018 (0.014-0.021); gains were minimal after including the discharge National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score. On 1,979 public coronary-trial fragments from the Aggregate Analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov (AACT), the software ran end to end, demonstrating its technical applicability to a second clinical text corpus. In conclusion, this workflow enables structured analysis of clinical registry free text and complements structured adverse-event documentation.
evidence_items.title: Decoding Complications: Large Language Model-Based Classification of Free-Text Entries in Clinical Stroke Registries

organizations: Hebei Normal University
Peking University
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Rolling bearings are critical components in industrial rotating machinery, and their failures may cause unexpected downtime, economic loss, and safety risks. Although deep learning and multimodal fusion have improved vibration-based fault diagnosis, two issues remain insufficiently addressed: magnitude-dominated time-frequency representations may discard phase-related impulse timing information, and heterogeneous diagnostic cues are often fused without explicit alignment in a semantically consistent representation space. This paper proposes M2-LLM-FD, a lightweight large language model-assisted framework for semantic-aware multimodal evidence integration in rolling bearing fault diagnosis. The framework converts each vibration segment into three complementary forms: time-domain patch tokens, phase-aware time-frequency tokens, and structured statistical prompts. A phase-preserving complex convolutional dimensionality reduction network is designed to process the real and imaginary components of the time-frequency representations, thereby retaining phase-sensitive information associated with fault-induced impulsive events. A structured multimodal alignment and fusion module then harmonizes temporal granularity and projects the aligned evidence into the pretrained language-model embedding space through semantic-anchor cross-modal attention. Furthermore, domain-specific prior knowledge is injected via structured statistical prompts, and the model is efficiently fine-tuned using Low-Rank Adaptation. \textcolor{red}{Extensive experiments on the CWRU, PU, and HUST datasets show that the proposed framework achieves consistent improvements in diagnostic accuracy, robustness, and cross-dataset generalization. Ablation and controlled analyses further validate the contributions of phase-aware time-frequency modeling, structured statistical prompts, and semantic-aware multimodal alignment to the overall diagnostic performance.
evidence_items.title: Semantic-aware multimodal evidence integration with a lightweight large language model for rolling bearing fault diagnosis

organizations: Melbourne Institute of Technology

Deakin University
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Liability for scam losses is shifting towards banks, yet few interpretable tools can anticipate which fraud and scam complaints will end in redress. This study develops SCAM-XD, an explainable framework that predicts whether a complaint to the US Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) flagged as possible fraud or a scam closes with monetary relief reported by the company. From the CFPB narratives archive, the study builds a benchmark of these complaints, about half of which human coders confirm as fraud or scams. A large language model (LLM) codes each narrative for scam type, payment rail, authorisation, manipulation cues and signals of the bank's response, agreeing closely with human coding on scam type. These features are combined with structured fields, company identity and text representations in a stacking ensemble, explained with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and linked to a cost-sensitive triage layer. Tested on a later period, SCAM-XD improves significantly on strong baselines across seeds, including a reimplemented topic model approach. LLM features yield a compact, interpretable model that nearly matches a high-dimensional text baseline but do not significantly improve the full model. Company identity is the strongest driver of predicted redress, yet firm identity alone predicts far less well, and payment rail and bank response cues act in directions consistent with liability rules. Under assumed costs, thresholds selected on validation data substantially reduce modelled expected cost relative to standard thresholds, whereas model choice matters much less. Redress depends on both the firm and the facts that determine liability.
evidence_items.title: An Explainable Machine Learning Framework with Large Language Model Features for Predicting Monetary Redress in Bank Fraud and Scam Complaints

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) could streamline research ethics and governance review by automating routine quality control checks. This study assessed Claude 3.5 Sonnet, ChatGPT4o, and Microsoft CoPilot in evaluating participant information sheets against Health Research Authority standards. Six clinical trial applications were processed using 32 standardised queries, with accuracy, processing time, error rates, and response quality assessed by two blinded reviewers. Claude showed the highest accuracy, detected more deviations from guidance, and had the fastest processing time (7.17 ± 0.68 min vs. ChatGPT 13.58 ± 2.2 min, CoPilot 23.25 ± 6.21 min). Hallucination rates were lowest in Claude, followed by ChatGPT and CoPilot. Claude also received the highest response quality ratings (77.6% “very good” vs. ChatGPT 56.7%, CoPilot 45.2%). While all three models were capable, Claude consistently outperformed the others, demonstrating the potential of LLM-assisted quality control while emphasizing the need for human oversight.
evidence_items.title: Evaluating large language models for quality control in research ethics review

organizations: Shariaty Technical College

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background: Differentiating between bipolar disorder (BD) and borderline personality disorder (BPD) is an intriguing clinical challenge that has attracted research attention, as the multiple co-occurring symptoms such as mood instability, impulsivity, and emotional dysregulation have made the boundary between the two disorders unclear. Recent research in computational psychiatry has shown promise in leveraging the power of knowledge graphs and large language models to enable accurate and inter­pretable decision-making. Methods: The study developed a hybrid framework, KG-Psy, that combines large language models with dynamic graphs. The system extracts clinical entities through GPT-5 while employing multi-step reasoning to find hidden connections within a psychiatric knowledge graph that weighs its evidence-based content. The system performs four main operations, which include extracting clinical entities, creating dynamic weighted knowledge graphs, using GPT-5 to trace multi-step cognitive pathways, and evaluating customized treatment options. The researchers used 310 anonymized psychiatric case re­ports to test their method. Results: KG-Psy achieved better discrimination between BD and BPD than other methods. The model achieved a maximum Precision (%) of 91.5, an improvement of 19%, 10.3%, and 7.4% over the KG-only, LLM-only, and Hybrid-other approaches, respectively. The system successfully discovered un­known cognitive pathways, which it used to create accurate pathway maps and provide treatment rec­ommendations supported by numerical evidence. The results of ablation experiments showed that LLM reasoning, combined with the knowledge graph structure, led to high performance.
evidence_items.title: A Knowledge Graph and Large Language Model Framework for Personalized Clinical Decision Support in Bipolar Disorder and Borderline Personality Disorder: The KG- Psy Framework

evidence_items.summary: Practice-oriented cybersecurity education often requires novice learners to build target web systems by hand before security analysis begins, imposing extraneous cognitive load. An earlier study introduced a Red/Blue teaming model in which a large language model (LLM) agent builds the target systems (vibe coding) under Human-on-the-Loop (HOTL) control, so that learners audit, attack, and defend. This single-cohort study examines learner-level evidence from the 2026 cohort (n = 34) of a university web-security course, set against institutional Course-Quality-Improvement (CQI) satisfaction records for nine of the ten academic years 2017–2026. Evidence comprised self-reported coding-effort logs (n = 25), single-item final-course survey measures (n = 27), and peer cross-evaluation scores (71 ratings). Logged total coding effort had a median of 3.8 h. In the final-course survey, 96% agreed implementation burden had decreased and 93% that deeper engagement in vulnerability analysis and defense design was possible (raw means 4.67 and 4.44 of 5; Wilcoxon p < 0.001). The 2026 CQI score (91.55) ranked second among the nine records (descriptive). In this single-institution context, delegating system construction to an LLM agent was associated with lower perceived implementation burden, greater reported security-analysis engagement, and high satisfaction; multi-site replication is required.
evidence_items.title: Cognitive Offloading with Large Language Model Agents in Cybersecurity Education: Perceived Burden and Engagement in a Single-Cohort Study with Ten-Year Institutional Context

evidence_items.summary: Patients and clinicians increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for return-to-sport decisions, but their reliability and the effect of structured clinical context remain uncertain. In this pre-registered, blinded, multi-model study, GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp answered 12 fictional anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction or lateral ankle sprain vignettes under instruction-only (Prompt+) and guideline-derived context (Context+) conditions across two runs, generating 192 outputs. Three blinded domain experts scored six binary criteria. The primary outcome was a correct clinical claim supported by a valid DOI or PMID. Context + did not improve the primary outcome compared with Prompt + (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.16–1.05; p = 0.065). GPT-5 was the only model whose point estimate favoured Context+, whereas the other three models favoured Prompt+. Claude Sonnet 4.5 showed a higher majority-vote Hallucination rate under Context + (22.7% vs 62.5%; Holm-adjusted p = 0.014); however, inter-rater agreement for Hallucination was poor (Fleiss’ κ < 0 in both domains), so this finding should be interpreted cautiously. Citation validity declined under Context + in three of the four models. Structured guideline-derived context did not reliably improve return-to-sport decision support in the models and conditions tested, and its effects varied between models. LLMs intended for clinical decision support should therefore undergo task- and model-specific evaluation before deployment.
evidence_items.title: Return to sport decision support with large language models after lower limb ligament injury

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Globally, marine pollution generated by oil spills, plastic litter, and industrial waste poses major threats to the environment, the economy, and human health. Field surveys, optical sensing, and manual sampling are examples of traditional monitoring and mitigation techniques that are frequently hampered by inefficiency, poor precision, and restricted coverage, particularly in large-scale or remote circumstances. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) hold revolutionary potential for detecting, managing, and monitoring maritime pollution. AI-based methods such as computer vision, deep learning, and machine learning have been effectively combined with drone imagery, remote sensing, and in situ monitoring to detect, classify, and measure plastic contaminants and oil spills with remarkable precision. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), transformer-based models, fuzzy systems, and neural networks have all improved pollutant detection, hotspot mapping, and predictive modeling while addressing challenges including noisy datasets and diverse environmental conditions. Furthermore, scalable solutions for real-time maritime waste detection and disposal are emerging from AI-driven autonomous systems that incorporate robotic mechanisms and Internet of Things (IoT) sensors. This study fully examines the current state of AI applications for marine pollutant identification, highlighting methodological advancements and detailing future potential for integrating AI into sustainable ocean monitoring and pollution management strategies.
evidence_items.title: Artificial intelligence for marine pollution monitoring and control

evidence_items.summary: AI is transforming education by providing immediate clarifications, tailored guidance, feedback and self-learning. This study has evaluated the awareness, use and perception of AI in mathematics education by students and compared the perception of male and female students. A descriptive survey was conducted by convenience sampling of participants. The data were collected both online and offline using a researcher-developed questionnaire, which had eight questions regarding students’ engagement with AI in mathematics education. Data were analysed by proportions. The results showed that the students knew about AI and valued its benefits in Mathematics education. Many students used AI for their learning, but a small portion of students used regularly for Mathematics, although many reported using it occasionally. Most of the students opted for AI platforms like Google Gemini, ChatGPT and others. Students primarily used AI for problem solving, exam preparation, and conceptual understanding. They also thought AI could make learning math easier and supported its use in their schools. Mathematics: Male students used AI more than female students. The findings show that AI is a powerful learning tool for students, but its educational use needs to be properly directed, responsibly used and critically verified for AI-generated mathematical answers.
evidence_items.title: Students’ Perceptions of Using Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Education

evidence_items.summary: The article describes a set of methods and algorithms that form the basis of artificial intelligence technologies and examines their characteristics and technical features of functioning in relation to solving tasks in criminalistics and forensic expertology. Based on the distinction between artificial intelligence technologies for “general” use and highly specialized technologies, the limits of their application in practical activities are defined.Using examples of “general” use technologies (ChatGPT, Alice AI, Grok, and Qwen Chat), their low effectiveness is demonstrated in terms of studying document details to identify the writing materials by the provided digital image of a handwritten text fragment as well as by the verbal description of a specific writing material as a combination of specific features.Based on the results of a comprehensive analysis of the experimentally obtained data, it is concluded that the technological capabilities of these tools in forensic examination are highly limited when solving tasks aimed at determining the reference group of writing materials. At the same time attention is drawn to the importance of using modern, highly specialized technologies developed for a specific expert task provided that the relevant software will not be the sole means of examination and will be used exclusively by the experts competent in their field and the results of such programs are evaluated based on the expert’s specialized knowledge.
evidence_items.title: On the Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence Technologies in Forensic Examinations

evidence_items.summary: Recent geopolitical disruptions, including trade wars, pandemics, and maritime bottlenecks, have intensified the need for supply chain resilience in the defense industry. Such shocks manifest as demand spikes and component shortages for specific products, in which material substitution is a viable strategy to ensure production agility. This, however, might result in unforeseen compromises in system performance and mission readiness due to incomplete system knowledge and hidden interdependencies. As such, this paper proposes an AI-driven product reconfiguration process to enable circular defense ecosystems, in which localized, closed-loop resource flows strengthen industrial resilience and reduce strategic dependencies. Grounded in product family design and system design principles, the workflow uses causal reasoning to evaluate reconfigurable product architectures and circular component pathways across the defense ecosystem. By integrating knowledge from designers, procurement, operations, and end users, the approach supports rapid assessment of the potential for circularity, the feasibility of reconfiguration, and trade-offs among performance, cost, and sustainability. The proposed method enhances decision agility under uncertainty and enables defense organizations to proactively adapt product families in response to disruptions. This transdisciplinary research contributes a novel intersection of the circular economy, ecosystem thinking, and AI-enabled reconfiguration to build resilient and adaptive defense industrial systems
evidence_items.title: Artificial Intelligence as an Enabler for Resilient Circular Defense Ecosystems

evidence_items.summary: The Local Skill Exchange Network is a proposed web-based platform designed to connect individuals who want to learn new skills with people who possess relevant knowledge and expertise. Traditional learning platforms often focus on structured courses, while local communities may have difficulty discovering nearby individuals who can provide personalized guidance or participate in reciprocal skill exchanges. The proposed system addresses this challenge by integrating skill discovery, location-based search, intelligent recommendations, session booking, real-time communication, online payments, and a skill barter mechanism into a unified application. Users can register as skill providers, learners, or both, create skill profiles, specify availability, and search for suitable learning opportunities. The recommendation module ranks potential matches using factors such as skill relevance, geographical proximity, ratings, price, experience, and availability. Google Maps integration supports geographical discovery, while a payment gateway facilitates paid sessions. The barter module enables users to exchange skills without requiring monetary transactions. Administrative and moderation modules support user management, content review, dispute handling, and platform analytics. The proposed application follows a modular monolithic architecture with a web frontend, backend REST APIs, and a relational database. The system aims to improve access to community-based learning, encourage knowledge sharing, and provide a scalable foundation for personalized skill development. Its effectiveness can be evaluated through functional testing, recommendation relevance, booking success rate, response time, and user feedback.
evidence_items.title: Small Language Models: The Future of On-Device Artificial Intelligence

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM) is the dominant surface-code decoder but is suboptimal under depolarizing noise, because it discards the X – Z correlation that Y errors induce and is not degeneracy-aware. We present an exactly anchored diagnostic benchmark for the code-capacity depolarizing channel, not a case for neural decoding. Five decoders (MWPM, correlated matching, belief-matching, belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding (BP+OSD) and a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP)) are compared with an exact analytic maximum-likelihood (ML) reference at distance d = 3 , with exact per-syndrome ML decisions on sampled syndromes at d = 5 , and with a matched-marginal independent-noise control. Measuring MWPM’s suboptimality by the relative logical-error-rate (LER) reduction that ML achieves over it, the difference between the depolarizing and control channels is 19–32 percentage points (pp) above an 11%–14% floor at d = 3 , and 33–60 pp above an 8%–10% floor at d = 5 . At d = 3 the MLP recovers 90%–95% of the MWPM-to-ML gap, more than belief-matching (82%–89%), BP+OSD (74%–80%) or correlated matching (46%–58%). At d = 5 belief-matching and BP+OSD agree closely yet stay measurably above ML, recovering 79%–91% of the gap, while the MLP’s advantage over MWPM depends on the training budget (crossover near 3.5 × 10 5 samples at p = 0.08 ) and, when adequately trained, recovers at most 17%. In simulated circuit-level memory experiments at d = 3 and 5, the classical decoders keep their advantage over MWPM, the matched-marginal split becomes decomposition-dependent, and the MLP recovers 25% of the gap at d = 3 , T = 2 and, over five training seeds and budgets up to 9 × 10 5 samples, stays an order of magnitude worse than MWPM at d = 5 , T = 5 , with or without validation-based early stopping. Per-shot cost grows 33–97-fold for the BP-based decoders but less than twofold for matching, and batched throughput does not bound latency.
evidence_items.title: Decomposing neural decoders: an exactly-anchored benchmark for quantum error correction

evidence_items.summary: The Apollo 12 landing near Surveyor 3 left measured damage on hardware that was returned to Earth. That damage is a rare test case for lunar plume-ejecta models. Modern Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) data place the lunar module (LM) 156.8 m from Surveyor 3, on ground about 10 m higher than Surveyor's. This report tests one specified, collision-free ballistic model family. Grains travel ballistically in vacuum over the measured terrain, and their launch angle may rotate with the local slope by a coupling fraction k. When launch is referenced to horizontal (k = 0), no grain reaches the camera at 100 m/s or faster in 200 terrain-error trials. A simple height calculation shows why. A grain launched horizontally can reach the camera only if it is slower than about 46 m/s (42.7 to 51.5 m/s across the height cases). This result excludes a direct horizontal sheet. It does not exclude horizontal launch followed by collisions or scattering. Slope-referenced launch does deliver fast grains. Couplings of k = 0.5 and 1.0 predict nearly the same pit density (864 and 842 pits/cm²). Both exceed the measured 103 pits/cm², and both need the same unmeasured attenuation to match it. With k limited to 0.4 to 1.0, at least one such equal-output pair survives in 34 of 40 terrain cases and 33 of 33 registration cases. The record therefore bounds k from below but does not fix it. Neither the 255:2 front-to-rear crater count nor the literal shadow bearing separates the two settings. No retained pair matches the literal historical bearing for both members, and only 38 of 610 meet the literal elevation interval. They do disagree elsewhere. Around a fixed Surveyor 3, 49 of 296 candidate landing cells 30 to 200 m away are exposed under one coupling but not the other. This is a model sensitivity, not a validated hazard limit or protection distance.
evidence_items.title: The Apollo 12–Surveyor 3 Plume-Ejecta Benchmark: Geometry and Identifiability Limits

organizations: Brac University
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Human-derived nucleic acids introduced during sample collection or laboratory handling are a longstanding concern in genomics. Sensitive, high-throughput sequencing can capture trace human nucleic acids, potentially exposing genetic information in nominally host-free microbial datasets. We systematically examined bacterial isolate sequencing archives and found frequent human-sequence contamination, with recurrence within projects and marked heterogeneity among libraries, including those sharing sequencing lanes. Human fragments spanned chromosomes and retained population-informative alleles, concordant partial allele states and clinically annotated variants. Computational depletion removed more than 99.99\% of strict human fragments, eliminating measured population-affinity and clinically annotated variant signals while largely preserving bacterial assembly features. Human contamination was also detected in bacterial RNA-seq, with both genome-alignable reads and splice-junction evidence of processed human transcripts. Together, these findings show how incidental human material can become recoverable genetic information in public microbial archives and underscore the need for screening before data deposition.
evidence_items.title: Recurrent human-sequence contamination and recoverable genetic information in bacterial sequencing archives

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Background Intravitreal injections are the most frequently performed intraocular procedure worldwide. Yet the 50 µL dose is usually delivered with syringes designed neither for volumes this small nor for injection into the eye. Dosing accuracy, particulate contamination and residual volume have previously been examined in separate studies, so trade-offs between these properties within a single syringe remain unclear. We assessed all three properties in the same syringes, including models in clinical use for intravitreal injection that have not been characterised previously. Methods Six syringes were evaluated: Injekt ® F Luer Solo 1 mL, Omnifix-F Luer Lock Solo 1 mL, Henke-Ject eco 1 mL (three-part), Zero Residual 0.2 mL, BD Micro-Fine 1 mL, and Omnican 50 U-100 insulin syringe. Dosing accuracy and precision for a 50 µL target volume was assessed with 23 specialist staff. The dosing data were analysed descriptively, and operator-dependent variability was quantified with a linear mixed model. Residual volume was determined according to DIN EN ISO 7886-1. Particulate contamination was quantified by light obscuration after 7-day incubation of water, with and without flicking of the syringe during filling. Particle counts were analyzed descriptively. Results All syringes tended to overdose, with a median delivered volume of 55.1 µL, and only 45.4% of the measurements were within 45–55 µL. In the mixed model, 22% of the variance of the delivered volume was attributable to between-operator differences, and no syringe type differed significantly in mean delivered volume. Among the syringes measured without a needle, the mean residual volume ranged from 0.18 µL to 23.1 µL; the two syringes with integrated needles showed 0.59 µL and 1.77 µL including the needle dead space. All syringes released particulate matter, and in this exploratory study the particle count was higher after flicking in five of the six syringe types.
evidence_items.title: Performance characterization of syringes used for intravitreal injections: dosing accuracy, particulate contamination, and residual volume

organizations: Diagnostic Imaging Center, Kuopio University Hospital, Kuopio, Finland.

evidence_items.summary: Background Use of open sources in nuclear medicine facilities demands reliable surface contamination measurements. Regulatory limits for contaminated areas are set at very low surface activity values, from 0.4 Bq cm -2 to 4 Bq cm -2 . Objective This study evaluates the sensitivity of two different contamination meters to detect low contamination values in clinical settings using radionuclides with different decay modes. Additionally, the effect of contaminated area size on sensitivity and quantitative accuracy was assessed. Methods Two types of contamination meters were used to measure four radionuclides with different decay modes: 223 Ra, 177 Lu, 99m Tc, and 18 F. The measurements were performed at two different distances (2 cm and 10 cm) and over two surface areas (1 cm 2 and 16 cm 2 ). Results At a 2 cm distance and 16 cm 2 surface area, the lowest detectable surface activity was 2 Bq cm -2 for alpha- and beta-emitting radionuclides, whereas for 99m Tc it was above 1 kBq cm -2 . Quantitative accuracy was the highest for 177 Lu with surface activity between 5.0–12.5 Bq cm -2 , ranging from 1.1% to 20.9%. For the smaller surface area (1 cm 2 ), detection limits were substantially higher: 1 MBq cm -2 for 99m Tc and 40 Bq cm -2 for 223 Ra, 177 Lu, and 18 F. Conclusion Measurement sensitivity and accuracy depend strongly on radionuclide decay mode and contaminated area size. Small, concentrated contaminations are detectable only at sufficiently high surface activity whereas lower surface activity values become detectable when the size of the contaminated area increases. Importantly, contamination meters demonstrated optimal performance for alpha and beta emitters, which represent the most significant contamination risk in clinical practice.
evidence_items.title: Evaluation of Contamination Meter Efficiency for Detecting Surface Activity Across Decay Modes and Contaminated Area Sizes in Clinical Settings

organizations: POLYTECH Maradi, University of Maradi
evidence_items.summary: Abstract Sizing a mini-grid well still leaves open how to run it the next morning. Using the quality-controlled 2015–2024 record of three Nigerien stations (Agadez, Bilma, N'Guigmi), we forecast daily sunshine one to seven days ahead and 3-hourly wind speed three to 72 hours ahead with gradient boosting (HGB) and a compact neural network against persistence and SARIMA, training on 2015–2022, testing on 2023–2024, and confirming the comparison over six rolling years (2019–2024). Both beat persistence by a wide margin (RMSE skill 18–49 percent for wind, 15–30 percent for sunshine), but the margin over SARIMA is thin and site-dependent: HGB beats SARIMA for wind at every lead at Agadez in 2023–2024, though it narrows over the rolling years, is most consistent at Bilma, and is not significant at N'Guigmi. Heat-stress and wind-regime features change RMSE by about 1 percent or less for wind and up to 5.4 percent for sunshine, short of the hypothesised Harmattan gain; cross-site pooling lowers Agadez's 24-h wind RMSE by 3.1 percent when data are scarce. Raw quantile forecasts at Agadez are miscalibrated (67–72 percent coverage for nominal 80 percent intervals); conformal recalibration improves this to 76–82 percent but drifts across years. For an illustrative 100 kWp PV plus 30 kW wind plant, a better forecast lowers the CVaR95 battery buffer at Agadez from 342 to 235 kWh, narrowed further by propagating wind quantiles through the power curve. The gains are real but modest, site-dependent, and the honest measure of what an operator can count on tomorrow.
evidence_items.title: Day-Ahead Forecasting of Sunshine and Wind for a Dust- and Heat- Prone Hyper-Arid Mini-Grid: Machine Learning against Persistence and SARIMA at Agadez, Bilma and N'Guigmi, Niger (2015-2024) A real-data benchmark with regime-aware features, cross-site transfer and conformal calibration

evidence_items.summary: Although early stages of product development have the high potential to influence sustainability outcomes, they are also marked by a high level of uncertainty and a lack of reliable lifetime data. This gap hinders the evaluation of environmental implications and causes late-stage redesigns. This study offers a data-driven approach that combines AI-supported predictive analytics for sustainability-oriented decision-making with sovereign data ecosystems. It maintains data sovereignty while facilitating cross-organizational sharing and reuse of sustainability information. AI models are used to estimate missing or ambiguous data, enabling early assessment of environmental consequences, incl. Product Carbon Footprints, prior to the availability of comprehensive product specifications. Standardized connectors, Asset Administration Shells, and digital product passports are examples of interoperable technologies, which are integrated into the Manufacturing X data space architecture. The viability of cross-dataspace interoperability is confirmed by a demonstrator, allowing safe and reliable data transfer across diverse ecosystems. The findings demonstrate how Product Lifecycle Management may be integrated with data ecosystems and predictive analytics to support ongoing monitoring of business and regulatory sustainability objectives. This enables businesses to make sustainability a proactive design parameter rather than a reactive restriction. This strategy reduces development risks, improves value chain transparency, and supports more effective and circular product engineering techniques in distributed industrial ecosystems.
evidence_items.title: Data-Driven and AI-Supported Product Development for Sustainability Within a Data Ecosystem

evidence_items.summary: Abstract Deep-learning structure predictors (AlphaFold2, ESMFold) require global context. Modeling outer membrane protein (OMP) loops without transmembrane scaffolds creates an out-of-distribution challenge. Across 28 non-redundant OMP crystal structures (1.40–3.10 Å), isolated loops collapsed, inverting core solvent accessibility (native core RSA: 3.6 ± 0.7% inverted to 58.7 ± 4.5% [AF2] and 62.1 ± 4.8% [ESMFold] for buried positions; mean loop RSA: 32.1 ± 10.0%), yielding 0.00% true negative rate (0/28 retaining core burial; 95% Clopper–Pearson CI: [0.00%, 10.15%]) across RSA thresholds 5%–20%. Intact models preserved burial (AF2: 27/28 [96.43%], residue TNR 96.89% ± 5.6%; ESMFold: 26/28 [92.86%], residue TNR 93.21% ± 4.2%). Mean pLDDT fell from 83.0 ± 5.1 to 66.9 ± 4.8, correlating with backbone Cα RMSD (r = − 0.68, p < 0.001; 4.83 ± 1.92 Å); 27/28 intact proteins (96.4%) maintained pLDDT > 70. Mixed-effects modeling confirmed core RSA increases (β = +28.5%, p < 0.0001). A backbone-centric Cα contact density filter (CDα ≤ 10.17; ≤ 10 neighbors at rc = 8.0 Å) identified exposed loops, achieving pilot residue-level macro-averaged AUC of 0.80 ± 0.08 (pooled AUC = 0.96; n = 3 test proteins). Prioritized Pseudomonas aeruginosa epitopes were assembled into a 93-residue chimera. Explicit-solvent molecular dynamics (4 systems × 5 × 300 ns; 6.0 µs CHARMM36m + 6.0 µs Amber ff14SB = 12.0 µs total; 6.0 µs/force field) preserved epitope exposure (41.8 ± 1.2 vs. 28.3 ± 3.1 nm²; Cohen’s d = 4.8). Predictors require intact scaffolding for OMP loop modeling; CDα provides an exploratory filter for full-length prioritization.
evidence_items.title: Structural Context Collapse in Deep-Learning Predictors: A Benchmark of Outer Membrane Protein Loop Decontextualization and a Backbone-Centric Filter for Surface Epitope Identification

evidence_items.summary: Historic urban destinations contain culturally significant places whose digital visibility, accessibility, and suitability for visitation vary substantially. This paper presents Agentic SHIFT, the Smart Heritage Itinerary Framework for Transmission, a context-aware multi-agent framework for auditable cultural heritage itinerary recommendation. Nine specialised agents coordinate visitor profiling, context modelling, heritage retrieval, operational eligibility, heritage and under-exposure scoring, expected suitability, pedestrian routing, evidence-bounded narration, and visual verification. The Marrakech benchmark contains 196 cultural POIs across ten heritage categories. Twenty calibration configurations were used to select the utility weights, and forty held-out paired configurations were used for the final comparison. On the held-out set, Agentic SHIFT achieved mean heritage coverage of 0.757, digital under-exposure of 0.767, cultural diversity of 0.522, expected suitability of 0.631, and a mean walking distance of 1.973 km. Relative to popularity ranking, it increased heritage coverage by 0.047 and digital under-exposure by 0.448 while reducing walking distance by 0.375 km. Removing the operational gate reduced operational validity from 1.000 to 0.696. Two stored OSMnx routes confirmed pedestrian-network execution within a four-hour budget. A documentary audit of thirteen narrative claims found eleven directly supported claims and two claims retained with explicit qualification, while a detailed audit of four visual records confirmed identity, creator, licence, and publication-suitable resolution for all four audited images.
evidence_items.title: Agentic SHIFT: A Multi-Agent AI Framework for Visual and Context-Aware Cultural Heritage Exploration

evidence_items.summary: Quantum circuits are central to implementing quantum algorithms on quantum devices, where quantum gates must be reversible. Many quantum algorithms rely on Boolean functions, which must therefore be implemented reversibly within quantum circuits. Reversible circuit synthesis provides a way to translate such Boolean functions into reversible circuits. Binary decision diagrams (BDDs) offer a scalable approach to this task, but the resulting BDDs and circuits depend heavily on variable ordering. Existing ordering heuristics commonly minimize BDD size because it is closely tied to the circuit size. However, BDD size is an imperfect proxy for the quantum cost of the synthesized circuit (QCC). We propose \texttt{QuantumEvo}, an evolutionary framework that uses an LLM as a heuristic generator for QCC-aware BDD variable ordering. Instead of predicting orderings directly, \texttt{QuantumEvo} searches over ordering heuristics initialized from multiple heuristic families. Candidate heuristics directly manipulate variable orderings using standard BDD operations and are selected by downstream QCC. The discovered heuristic, HGA-QE, modifies the sifting step inside a genetic algorithm so that the procedure is better aligned with QCC. Across the benchmark set, HGA-QE achieves a 70.9\% tie-or-win rate against the per-function best baseline and is strictly best on 13.5\% of the functions. The results demonstrate broadly competitive QCC performance, with HGA-QE showing a clearer relative advantage in strict wins on the two benchmark suites drawn from sources different from the data used for heuristic discovery.
evidence_items.title: LLM-Driven Algorithm Design for Quantum Circuit Synthesis based on Binary Decision Diagrams

evidence_items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) holds great promise for clinical support, particularly in ophthalmology, where retinal fundus photography is essential for diagnosis. However, ophthalmic VQA benchmarks primarily emphasize answer accuracy, neglecting the explicit visual evidence necessary for clinical interpretability. In this work, we introduce FundusGround, a new benchmark for clinically interpretable ophthalmic VQA with spatially-grounded lesion evidence. Specifically, we propose a three-stage pipeline that collects 10,719 fundus images with 15,595 image-level meticulously annotated lesions. To ensure anatomical consistency and clinical validity, all lesions are spatially localized using the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) grid, enabling standardized mapping to nine clinically meaningful retinal regions. Built upon this structured lesion evidence, 72,706 questions are then generated spanning four formats: open-ended, closed-ended, single-choice, and multiple-choice. We further benchmark multiple general- and medical- large vision-language models using dual metrics for answer accuracy and lesion-level reasoning. The experiments demonstrate that incorporating lesion-level visual evidence consistently improves model performance and transparency, highlighting the necessity of explicit spatial grounding for reliable and explainable ophthalmic VQA.
evidence_items.title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Ophthalmic VQA via Spatially-Grounded Lesion Evidence

INTEGRATED QUANTUM-NANO HONEYCOMB SUSTAINABLE CIVILIZATION FAMILY 40 / F196-F200 | SCIENTIFIC & TECHNICAL NOTEBOOK | RESEARCH WORKING EDITION v1.0 33 x STARLI / WHITE RAINBOW RESEARCH LIBRARY This final research family does not claim that civilization-scale autonomy is achievable today. Five separate prospective questions are tested: practical quantum computing in nanorobotic manufacturing; independently qualified factoryless honeycomb repair; safe services for sustainable habitats; resource ledgers with a physical human stop; and cross-laboratory reproducibility of a whole-system future research benchmark. The point of the book is to leave a testable door, not an unfalsifiable promise. No figure in this edition is an observed quantum speedup, tested nanofactory, occupied habitat, or licensed civic infrastructure. THE FIVE SOURCE-ANCHORED FLAGSHIPS F196 | Integration of Quantum Computing and Nanorobotic Swarm Manufacturing at the Limit | 量子計算與奈米機器人集群製造整合的極限 F197 | Integration of Honeycomb Self-Regeneration and Factoryless Production at the Limit | 蜂巢自主再生與無工廠生產融合的極限 F198 | Quantum–Nano Robotics for Sustainable Living Civilizations at the Limit | 量子奈米機器人與永續居住文明協同的極限 F199 | Resource Circularity and Trustworthy Autonomy in Regenerative Civilization Platforms at the Limit | 自動再生文明資源閉環與可信自主平台的極限 F200 | Future Research on Quantum Honeycomb Autonomous Regenerative Civilizations at the Limit | 量子蜂巢自動再生永續文明未來研究的極限 THE FORTY-FAMILY COUPLING FRAMEWORK AND SCIENTIFIC INHERITANCE Families 1-8 provide local coordination and distributed manufacturing concepts; families 9-16 introduce quantum, nanoscale and programmable materials hypotheses; families 17-24 test honeycomb architectures, repair, energy, water and ecological regeneration; families 25-32 add independent habitability, food, materials, microgrids, public services, disaster recovery and digital-twin witnesses; families 33-40 examine quantum assistance, nano-honeycomb materials, regenerative manufacturing, urban infrastructure, resource optimization, trustworthy governance, human-robot co-evolution and final integration. These are interfaces for testing, not certificates that one domain validates another. A service certificate must not travel across domains without evidence. An accepted robotic joint cannot certify drinking water; a functioning water service cannot demonstrate civil rights; a signed permission token cannot prove the motor stopped; and a quantum solver returning a good score cannot prove nanomanufacturing advantages. The architecture is meaningful precisely because these distinctions are separately recorded and falsifiable. FIVE-STAGE PARALLEL RESEARCH CONTROL SYSTEM 1 / Freeze research DNA: lock five official F196-F200 titles, the 915-page mother-work conceptual chapter lineage, distinct physical endpoints, system safety envelopes, classical strong controls and human authority constraints. 2 / Formalize mechanisms: connect 30 dimensioned candidate relations to testable material and service endpoints; generate 42 deterministic synthetic 3D response tables with CSV, Python and full parameters, not fabricated field observations. 3 / Reconstruct independent witnesses: for each chapter use calibrated physical acceptance, blind quality tests, full material and energy ledgers, confirmed human permission and reproducible timestamps; clearly separate a virtual test from a real one. 4 / Challenge competing worlds: include equal-budget classical quantum-comparison baselines, conventional repair networks, human-operated sustainable habitats, public auditing and counterfactual resource accounting. Every research door must permit a negative result. 5 / Audit and permit transfer: check engineering dimensions, figure recomputation, text layout, independent chapter progression, distinctive research gates and prototype stop tests before publication; successors may discard unsupported claims. SOURCE LINEAGE AND EVIDENCE CEILING The supplied 915-page SWARM MANUFACTURING AND ROBOTIC MATTER AT THE LIMIT research mother provides conceptual chapters 17 (Task Allocation Without a Central Foreman), 45 (Scaffolded and Scaffold-Free Construction), 63 (Self-Repairing Robotic Structures), 64 (When the Product and the Factory Become the Same System), 65 (Construction Swarms in the Built Environment), 66 (Disaster-Zone Fabrication and Repair), 71 (Infrastructure Maintenance by Distributed Agents), 73 (Scaling Laws for Million-Agent Manufacturing), 75 (Energy Economics of Distributed Production), 77 (Digital Twins for Multi-Robot Manufacturing), 79 (Standards, Interoperability, and Handoff), 81 (Robotic Matter as Civilizational Infrastructure) and 82 (Toward a Manufacturing Ecology of Autonomous Matter). The mother is not evidence that the five novel hypotheses have passed independent experiments.
